_comment_about_this_template: Gemini CLI commands are JSON entries in .gemini/gemini_cli_config.json under the top-level 'commands' object. This file demonstrates the shape of a single entry. Copy the inner object into your gemini_cli_config.json's commands map, keyed by the command name (slug). DO NOT ship the wrapper around this object literally; consume only the entry shape.

<command-slug>.command: echo 'Replace this with the actual shell command to run'
<command-slug>.description: <One-line description of what this command does. Shown in Gemini's command picker.>
<command-slug>.directory: <optional working directory; omit for repo root>

_additional_example_run_tests.description: Run all frontend tests using the default test runner.

_field_reference.command: Required. The shell command to execute. Use a single string; for multi-step operations, write a small wrapper script in scripts/ and reference it here.
_field_reference.description: Required. One concise line for the command picker.
_field_reference.directory: Optional. Working directory relative to the repo root. Omit for repo root.

_anti_patterns: Don't put a multi-line shell pipeline directly in 'command' — write a script and call it.
Don't shadow built-in slash commands without a clear reason.
Don't include secrets in 'command' — they'll appear in shell history.
Don't use this for interactive workflows — those are skills (Claude Code) or skills with user-invocable=true (Codex). Gemini doesn't have a separate skill primitive.
